Water boils at **100°C** (212°F) at standard atmospheric pressure at sea level.

This is because the atmospheric pressure at sea level is defined as 1 atmosphere (101.325 kPa or 760 mmHg), and at this pressure, water's vapor pressure equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure at 100°C, allowing bubbles of water vapor to form within the liquid and rise to the surface—what we observe as boiling.
